Uflex C5X08 C5 Engine Control Cables for Mercury & Mercruiser, 8' So the image on this ad is obviously not the product for sale. 6+ months after verifying this with the seller, the wrong image is still in place. Seller is great though. Ordered 2 of these in April '21 and finally got around to fitting them in October '21 only to find out one of the cables was a 20' cable. Even though I was well out of return window, TX Parts LLC stood behind their sale and sent me the correct part and a label to return the wrong one.
As for the part itself, it is the correct part for my 1986 Mercury 9.9hp outboard, but the round plastic cylinders that lock into place inside the engine are slightly off in their shape. The small cylinders in the new cables are the same overall length as the originals, but the new ones have flat ends and the original parts have a slight dome end to them. Due to this, the new cables will not lock into place. However, a quick sanding of the edges of the cylinder to make it a dome shape and it fits perfectly. Even with this small hassle it is well worth it for the price. I would buy these cables again and I would definitely buy from TX Parts LLC again.
text_fidelity_b: Uflex C5X08 C5 Engine Control Cables for Mercury & Mercruiser, 8'

text_fidelity_a: NordicTrack Commercial Studio Cycle Purchased this bike on 23 March.  Rode it 4 times before it failed.  Want to say that Amazon customer service has been very good.  The technician (that arrived today, 19 April) was very good.  NordicTrack from a product and customer support perspective was absolutely horrible.  First NT customer support tech had me hold my phone up to the bike to listen to the noise it was making.  Based on that assessment they determined the bike needed a replacement motor.  Waited two weeks for the part and, as stated, third party vendor technician was here today.  He disassembled the bike and after examining the situation determined that the motor was fine, the problem existed within the main "motherboard".  He mentioned that he has serviced several of this particular brand of bikes and witnessed multiple issues.  Again, Amazon support - excellent (provided scheduled pick up and refund go off without a hitch).  The technician - excellent.  NordicTrack - horrible, worthless.  Truly disappointed in a company that for 20+ years I understood to have a good reputation.  No more.  Would suggest that Amazon not carry this product (or ProForm which apparently is made by the NordicTrack people).
text_fidelity_b: NordicTrack Commercial Studio Cycle

text_fidelity_a:
Schwinn Fitness 430 Elliptical Trainer [Discontinued] I researched ellipticals for quite a while before ordering the Schwinn 430. My friend, Tom, also researched this type of equipment until his eyes fell out of his head. He wound up buying the Sole for about twice the cost of the Schwinn. In any event, he recommended the Schwinn as a good buy for the price. I then read just about all 400 Amazon reviews and FINALLY made my purchase.
I ordered my Schwinn 430 from Amazon on 3/1/10 and it was delivered on 3/8/10. I was delighted that it was delivered so fast and also happy about the free shipping.
My machine was delivered by ABF Freight Co. I know that some reviewers have complained about the shipping company but I had no problems at all. The driver was wonderful. He took the box down a small hill to the back of my house, up two steps onto the deck and then into the house. He was great!!!!!
It took Tom about 1-1/2 to 2 hours to put the machine together. He had just recently put together his Sole and so the parts were recognizable to him although I nearly passed out when I saw the photo of all the parts in the manual. Tom said that the manual was straight forward although there was an addendum for a particular washer. We didn't see that until I said "hey, what's this piece of paper saying?" All the pieces were accounted for and all the holes lined up perfectly. He used some of his own tools but used the supplied allen wrench where indicated. We didn't lube the parts as recommended by some reviewers.
I've used it for 3 days now and there is not a squeak to be heard, except for the creaking of my knees. I'm 5'7" and about 150 lbs and the 18" stride is fine for me. I'm a former runner and in good shape (I thought). I have the elliptical on level 1 and after 20 minutes, I've worked up a good sweat.
I agree that a backlight for the computer would have been nice but it's not a deal breaker for me. The 6 programs are more than enough.
I think this machine is well made and feels very solid. There is no rocking or moving. I have it on a carpet and did not buy a mat. I love that it has a small footprint. The longer machines would not have fit into the space alloted for the elliptical. For the price, it can't be beat. I highly recommend it.
I'll post again in a month to let you know if there is any squeaking. It's been almost 3 months now and I still love the machine. No squeaking at all. Good workout and still happy with my purchase. It did develop a squish (not a squeak) but then worked itself out.
text_fidelity_b: Schwinn Fitness 430 Elliptical Trainer [Discontinued]

Sawyer Products SP2129 Micro Squeeze Water Filtration System, 1 Pack, Black/Blue One thing you don't want to scrimp on is water filtering when you're hiking. Sawyer has an excellent reputation in the field, and we've used a different Sawyer filter for two years quite happily. This is a nice addition to their line-up.

Pros:
Size: it's small, compact, and quite light

Easy to use: screw it on to the included 32 0z. bladder once you've filled it, onto most regular types of disposable plastic water bottles (but please don't use those!), onto many bladders, or use the included straw to drink from the water source directly (though less comfortably). That's it.

Water flow: It comes out quickly enough to drink directly without any annoying pause or lag (you can also squeeze the bag for more flow).

Drinking bag feels quite durable, always a concern for these sorts of filters. I wouldn't be worried about this one.

Comes with an extra gasket, straw, and cleaning syringe

Backflushing is easy and quick

Quasi-negatives
Doesn't do viruses. I don't consider this a real negative since a) if you're hiking in the US you don't need to worry about viruses and b) if you're looking for something to take care of viruses you're looking for a real step up in price and product so that's a whole different category

No instructions. This is more just a little annoying, but easily solved by going online and looking at the videos.

It's a great little product from a trustworthy source. Water filters have come a long way from the old bulky pump action and so if you're still using one of those, consider moving up to something like this. So much easier and better to carry.

text_fidelity_a:
POC, Ventral Air MIPS Road Cycling Helmet with Performance Cooling We recently got an electric scooter, plus my wife rides roller blades, and we’re talking about an electric bike - or recumbent, not sure which. We have a need for a couple bike helmets. I will fully admit, we are NOT experts in this area and have done no research beyond knowing they need to be rated and that there are good ones and bad. We have each owned in the past - that kind that looks similar to this, but with that point at the back, which always makes us think, what happens if you land on the back and that point slams the helmet forward...

So when I had the chance to grab this POC Ventral Air MIPS (CPSC) I took it without hesitation. Not only does it look good, but in wearing it, it feels great and gives us a sense of being safer than without a helmet. And for all the helmets we have owned, that this has the blunted back, answers that “what if,”

So this POC Ventral Air MIPS (CPSC) arrived and we broke in right away - had to see it in person. We were blown away by the presentation - it comes in a nice box - make sure to take care of this box, it is your storage box! Inside you’ll find the helmet and a bag. Open up and the helmet goes in the bag in the box - it is a GREAT way to store your helmet! Our previous helmets always end up on a shelf somewhere. This is excellent and we were already impressed.

Next... the helmet. It looks cool. Not only the color - I’m a blue guy and it’s perfect - but the overall design is so cool. We both liked the matted look - over the glossy really - but in person it looks even better. And on, it looks seriously cool. I tried it with both my reading glasses - no point other than to see how well it handles glasses - and my sunglasses - one of several I own, so one design style - and in both cases they fit perfectly under the sides of the helmet. I felt like I could wear them for an hour and have no rub or discomfort. I have not actually worn them out riding yet, but in this situation, the test was impressive.

As to that idea we always wondered about - what happens if you land on the back and that point - this is blunted, meaning there is no point. You land and it makes sense - you’ll have the back side make contact, but in a way that appears it’ll cushion the head and not shove it or the helmet forward.

The helmet is really light weight and you cannot believe how it feels like it could be that light and protect your head. So we put it on... and for me it fit perfectly. I got the large due to my large head. I had to open the strap slightly, but one half turn on the wheel and it was perfect - snug, but not tight nor uncomfortable. Now we only have this one, so when my wife went out to test the scooter, she had to wear this one. She has a much smaller head than mine, but it was nothing to size this down for her - while she technically doesn’t fit their size chart at this size, it worked well - she was comfortable and felt completely secure in it. It was very easy to size down for her, then bring it back up for me. It was easy and quick and we both felt great with it on.

I’ll be honest - this price point is above what we would normally spend. I was able to get it as a Vine Reviewer and for that I am grateful. I normally do not speak to price because of that, but in this case, wish to address it. In talking about it, we WOULD spend the money to get a second one for her. We feel that the safety this “promises” is worth the money. Now that said, We would do much more research first - we are not experts on the safety aspects of helmets and would make sure first. There is NO way we would go out and test this - meaning risk our head to see that is does what it promises. But if our further research shows what we think it would, yes, we would consider spending the money. Brain safety is important and we want something good. Now that said, if there is a product at a lower price that provides equal safety, we would seriously consider that - money is something we are careful with, but so too our safety. In the end, this is an excellent helmet that fits well and comfortably. Safety is the priority. But we do have to be realistic about cost. So if we could afford it and our research indicates it is a value, then yes, we would pay, but if not, if we found something as good at a lower price point, we’d have to look in that direction.

But we both love this POC Ventral Air MIPS (CPSC) helmet and are thrilled to have it.
text_fidelity_b: POC, Ventral Air MIPS Road Cycling Helmet with Performance Cooling

Magicmode Carbon Badminton Racket Set-with 6 Shuttlecocks and 1 Bag We have enjoyed playing badminton in a club setting, but due to Covid, have been unable to get back. So we decided to get a set for ourselves at home - as well as a net - and still be able to play. This set includes: a bag, 2 rackets, and container of 6 shuttlecocks. I would call this a set ideal for families, the backyard, beach, or picnics, but not for someone at the intermediate or advanced play/club play.

This is a great set. We got two nets here on Amazon for different settings, and took this set to our community tennis court.

The Bag: This is a great bag for this set. It allows one to carry both rackets and the tube of included shuttlecocks. That said, it would be a little better if the bag were even an inch longer. These are a tight fit at the current size. Even without the tube, these rackets have to be in essence pushed in in order to fit. But overall it's a great bag, looks great, and makes carrying easy.

The Rackets: These are nice. Again, this price point, these rackets are for family or couples looking for an hour of fun in the backyard, picnic, or on the beach - not a club setting. They have that nice sound when they connect, and they have a great distance on them. Lightweight, there was no fatigue after an hours play.

The Shuttlecocks: This is a great tube - 6 included. They are feathers, so nicer than the plastic kind. They get a nice sail to them. As feather, these will be damaged quickly, but one can continue to play for a good amount of time. We used one for a few games before needing to trade out. Plastic ones, once damaged, tend to need to be changed more quickly - in my experience.

This is a great set and for the right setting and players, perfect. We are happy and happy to recommend.

I miss out when she goes and was trying to think of ways I might still be able to go. I started seeing these eScooters and thought... why not? Had the chance to get one a couple of weeks ago and grabbed it. A short time later I would have the chance to get a second and grabbed it as well, allowing us both to use them when she's not blading.

We like both. Each has a couple "cons," but nothing we can't get over or around. And in the end, we really like them - both. They are each great fun to ride, easy to learn, and have let us enjoy some fun evening rides. Here's our take:

1. Our arrived in the very large box, folded, and needing some assembly before use.

2. There was sadly some damage to the box upon arrival, but didn't notice until - as we worked on the data box - that something seems to have poked a hole through the box, the interior stuffing, the instructions, and finally the end of the handlebars, leaving a gash in the material. It's disappointing, though we do not think caused any damage to how works. We worry about it getting wet in there - as parts to control the bike lie within - but we'll be careful. Though again, disappointing. It's not "brand new perfect."

3. The assembly was mostly easy. Pull up the handle into place, you do have to tighten/loosen/adjust with the included wrench that was truly not worth the cost of making it. One twice and it was slightly bent - but enough it wouldn't grip anymore. Had to use our own adjustable wrench. Got that worked out. Took a few adjustments, but it allows you to lock down the stick holding the handle bars. Once secure the stick and handles bars are very secure throughout the ride. The other eScooter we have allows the handlebars to drop down to fold in and carry in a bag - this does not - and while a nice feature, those also jiggle in a way that makes my wife unfordable while riding. I don't have a problem, but it is a consideration. So this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults makes for a smoother ride for my wife in that regard.

4. Once the stick and handlebars are locked into place, you're pretty much ready to go. It does go down, so you can store it folded, into a smaller piece. The rest of the footprint remains the same - meaning you only loose the height. We have left both open since assembly and find it is easy to get it in and out, but appreciate this feature. The one thing the other eScooter does is to fold down into a smaller overall package - though again, the same footprint size - and fits into an included carrying bag. This SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults does not do that. It is one feature that puts a point into the box for us with the other eScooter and not with this one. If you're working, going to school on a college campus, or maybe out for a ride and want to go in somewhere, being able to pack it into a bag and carry it is a nice feature this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults does not offer - though you can break it down and carry it by hand.

5. The SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults is also noticeably heavier than the other eScooter we got, but for each of us, not so much so we couldn't carry it a distance. You would notice the weight more quickly on this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults, but to/from a house, car, or the like it's easy enough.

6. The deck here is pretty decent - size, shape, and traction. My wife feels comfortable on it, but has said a little more room would be nice. But these are eScooters and designed for being useful, but not big. Ironically I'm a bit bigger than her and I am fine - though note the size on both - but ride the smaller other one. Because...

7. With a bit of added weight, I currently do not fit within the posted weight limit of this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults - which is decidedly lower than the other eScooter. Therefore, for safety, I have not even tried this one yet. My wife rides it and does love it. However, the weight difference is interesting in that this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults IS larger and a bit heavier, but the other one comfortably takes my weight in it's posted limits. So it's a bit weird. We feel like this one would likely be fine as well, but won't try. But it also puts another check in the box for the other one.

8. Great bell. Decent light. We both feel like the bell - which sounds similar to a bike bell - is far better on this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults, but the light are better on that one. This is doable, but not as large or as bright.

9. There are included tools for assembly, but again, the wrench was worthless after one turn, the others fine. We tossed the wrench, but kept the others if we need to adjust anything.

10. The range on this and the speed are great. I can't tell you off the top of my head what either are listed as, but we've been out and about over a few nights and gone a bit further each time. We're GenX and desk jockeys, so our activity levels had taken a dive - injuries and flu knocked us off our higher actives over the last year or so, though ironically not due to Covid. But getting on these has been a bit of a pacing task. We have been having to adjust to the standing in such a small spot and not moving - no room - so our feet are a bit... they are adjusting. It's been working and each ride we have been more and more comfortable - to the point we no longer stop for our feet being sore. Anyways, the point being, we are both still on the original charge, and we have gone some good distance as we learn and have fun. So we have not charged it yet to know how long. But we are very impressed with the distances we have so far gotten.

11. The speeds are excellent. Again, I've been riding the other one, but my wife easily keeps up. On that one I noticed my current weight does not limit my speed. That one has three speed levels and I'm in the middle. I THINK this one does as well and that she too is using the middle option. Her weight - well within the range of this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults - is no obstacle for her or this eScooter - she can go fast and feel it. We have done some decent "hill" climbing and decent and there is no struggle.

12. The Breaks - WORK! You STOP and you STOP! I mean, hit the breaks and she says it STOPS! The other one has a more reducing speed element - you push the button and it slows you, then you STOP with your feet. In her use of both eScooters, she actually prefers mine - the slowing rather than the STOP. She feels it's far TOO strong and she has to be careful of this so as not to knock herself off. It's not bad - not like she won't use it or is scared of using it - but the reducing speed almost feels like it gives her more control. We have not - yet and hopefully never - had a need to just STOP, but if we did, she's golden.

13. But the reducing speed on the other one allows me to go into controlled corners without stopping, but rather controlling the eScooter. I have a far wider range of speed levels it gives me to do intricate and controlled movements, rather than having to let it "naturally" slow down and do the same on this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults. So two different experiences of control in this way.

In the end, this is a REALLY FUN and well built eScooter. My wife loves it and I look forward to being able to try it when the weight is back down. In the mean time, we can both get out there, go for rides, and have fun. We are thrilled to have it. But... if we had to pick a single eScooter type/make to have, we both agree, we'd likely pick the other one. There is nothing they could have done - again, we feel it was a delivery issue - about the damage to the handlebar. It's disappointing, but we do not hold the eScooter or company responsible.

So that leaves the idea the other one can be broken down and carried in a bag, this one only broken down. This one IS a bit heavier. This one is a bit more of a process to put the handlebars up and down. This one does not have the same weight restrictions as the other - by a long shot of at least 30 lbs difference - meaning larger folks are more limited - check before you buy how much it can hold - so this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults one right away eliminated me from using it until I get these pounds back off. And the STOPPING of this being so abrupt is not our preference.

But in the end, we still truly love this eScooter. It IS a great ride and we have had fun being out. My wife is enjoying it very much. Would we pick the other if we had to? Yes. But for an eScooter, this one is really nice. We cannot - at present - give it anything less than 5 stars for what it does do - meaning we wouldn't drop any stars because of what it doesn't. We're happy to have this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults.
text_fidelity_b: SmooSat SA3(Prime) Electric Scooter for Adults, 20/28 Miles Long Range, 350W Brushless Motor, 8.5/10” Solid Tire, 15.6/20 MPH Max Speed, App Control &Type-C Reverse Charging(Prime Only), LED-Display

text_fidelity_a: DR.VIVA Fitness Tracker Watch, Heart Rate Activity Tracker Touch Color Screen IP67 Waterproof Sport Tracker Watch with Calorie Counter Pedometer Sleep Monitor for Kids Women Men I got this in exchange for my honest review.  This is a love hate relationship.  I love the features and all the different settings but I hate the interface.  Sometimes screens scroll super smooth and respond to touch inputs as they shoul and sometimes they wont scroll or lag so bad you want to smash this with a hammer.  Sometimes it links seamlessly with the phone and sometimes you canset it on top of the phone and it acts like it has never even haerd of bluetooth.  There is no rhyme or reason.  I used it in a workout yesterday and part way thru i must have bumped the screen because it turned off the fitness program.  Today it would not register i was working out at all.  Some of the data is super accurate (im wearing a second fitness watch just to compare) and some is so far off that according the the watch I may just be deceased (not really but i dont see my heartrate reaching 276 bpm just sitting watching videos)  The app is ok but does take some getting used to and some stuff that should be intuitive seems awkward and reversed.  They use odd terms for certian actions (like to unpair or disconnect from the phone they use the term unbind! )  There are a lot of nice features but are almost to specific (like there is no workout routine but you can choose tenmis, soccor, running, badmiton, basketball etc.).  And it stores messages (i thimk up to 5) but if you dont delete them new messages are not displayed only the old ones.  The band is real nice and the watch looks like a very expensive timepiece.  Charging was straight forward and batterylife was excellent.  The watch did get caught in an upgrade loop that kept telling us there was no devise connected.  We unbound and rebound the watch and it settled down.  There is a lot to do and set with this watch and when it is working it is really nice.  Patience is sometimes needed to work with it at times.  What i saw and used with this watch I really liked  and the app is a pretty good app once you get beyond some of awkward language
text_fidelity_b: DR.VIVA Fitness Tracker Watch, Heart Rate Activity Tracker Touch Color Screen IP67 Waterproof Sport Tracker Watch with Calorie Counter Pedometer Sleep Monitor for Kids Women Men

text_fidelity_a:
VELAZZIO Polarized Sunglasses for Men Women Fashion Sunglasses UV400 Protection Lightweight Good basic inexpensive sunglasses that block uv400 and are polarized. However, there are reviews on here saying these are a “high quality product.” These are good quality for the price point. But for this price obviously the frame is plastic, lenses are basic triacetate & can scratch easily, polarization film is on the outside of the lens which can degrade and are not very impact resistant.
Compare that to higher quality sunglasses (typically above $100) the lens material is likely to be polycarbonate. The polarized film is sandwiched between two layers of polycarbonate meaning the polarized film can never wear out and provides impact protection. That’s the big difference.
I like these glasses for just a basic pair to use for activities where I’m afraid to use my nicer sunglasses. Are these worth the price? Yes I believe these are a good value, have great looks and provide the basics. However, there are others out there for half this price that can provide the same basics but sometimes lack in style and fit.
I would say the glasses are a bit narrow on my face but I like the look and was surprised these were nicer than expected.
text_fidelity_b: VELAZZIO Polarized Sunglasses for Men Women Fashion Sunglasses UV400 Protection Lightweight

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Inspire Fitness Tracker, One Size (S and L Bands Included) I'm a long-time Fitbit user. I started out with my all-time favorite, the One, which was totally accurate and counted stairs. I replaced it with a Zip, which was also totally accurate but didn't count stairs, and mine went through batteries fast. I owned a couple Altas, that weren't accurate at all and I hated the charging cable.

And that brings me to the Inspire, which I'm pretty happy with. I'm going to start with the things I like about it.

I like the face options and how easy they are to change, the touchscreen - once you get used to it, it's very informative and easy to use, and I like the build quality, which is much nicer than the Zip for the same price I paid for the Zip a few years ago. I guess I got lucky - the unit uses about 10% of the battery per day. I very much prefer the way the Inspire docks in its charging cable - such an improvement over the Alta clips cable! And I've always had good luck getting support from Fitbit - when I had questions about the Inspire, I used their live chat and the rep was helpful and took her time.

Now for a neutral. My Inspire is reasonably accurate but not dead on. If I take 50 steps, it'll count 54 or 47. I can live with that. My One and Zip spoiled me, but both Altas were WAY off, which made me stop using a Fitbit for a while - no sense in wearing one if the counts are off by 25% to 30% (which they were).

There are cons. My first one only applies if you're a long-time Fitbit user and are used to using the wireless dongle so your Fitbit can communite with your computer. You won't be able to use the dongle because the Inspire uses Bluetooth rather than wireless to connect. I liked syncing with my computer, but opted to just sync with my phone as you now have to create a Microsoft account in order to download Fitbit Connect.

I found the band impossible to put on, but I mostly wear it on a clip, and there are some much easier to close and more attractive third-party bands for it on Amazon. It didn't recognize me cycling, and while that didn't bother me, it's worth noting - it would have been cool if that feature had worked.

My Inspire has made me a happy camper. I like wearing a Fitbit, seeing my steps and active minutes - that's why I've owned them. I find the Fitbit dashboard info and the quick stats on the screen motivating, and while I loved my One, the display on the Inspire gives more info more easily thanks to the touchscreen. I like the menus on the Inspire itself, the touchscreen and the charger. Oh, and I think the price ($58 when I bought it) is quite reasonable and a good value. I'm glad I got it :)
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Inspire Fitness Tracker, One Size (S and L Bands Included)

text_fidelity_a:
IRONMAN Exerpeutic 250 Manual Treadmill UPDATE Feb. 2016
I've changed my rating to 1 star. I think I was able to use this a total of 4 or 5 times before it died. You can see some of my experiences below in the original review. That creaking got louder, so I added a bit of WD40 into the roller (not the belt), which seemed to have solved the problem. Then at the end of last week, I was walking on it, and the thing suddenly froze up completely. Rollers won't move, belt won't move, nothing. It is DEAD.

To be fair, Paradigm (the manufacturer) did offer to replace the thing for me. But they had never even heard of this happening; I had no confidence that they really knew the product that well. If they replaced it, I'd have to pay for assembly AGAIN, and have no guarantee that the new machine wouldn't have the same problems. So we decided not to replace it with an Exerpeutic machine but go with a different brand entirely, and purchased from a local store that will give us support.

My original review:

I vascillated between giving this 3 or 4 stars. I like it, but am unsure about how long it will last. Firstly, we paid for the professional assembly and I'm glad we did because it took him over an hour to put it together. The packaging was poor, as other reviewers have said, and a couple of pieces were broken. One seemed to be a plastic bit that wasn't serving any purpose, so we cut it off with some tools.

In terms of workout, I like it quite a bit. Yes, the incline is fairly steep, but that's why I appreciate it; it's helps me break a sweat easily. The advantage of a manual is that you can speed up or slow down on your own time; you don't have to fiddle with buttons.

In terms of noise, it's louder than other Exerpeutic exercise equipment. In addition to the constant swishing sound, the treadmill creaks a fair amount. I'm hoping our downstairs neighbors won't be bothered (so far they haven't complained...we'll see). The creaking certainly doesn't instill confidence in the longevity of the product. But for the time being it's working and I'm grateful because we have a small apartment and could never fit a full-sized treadmill in here.
text_fidelity_b: IRONMAN Exerpeutic 250 Manual Treadmill

The light attaches to your handle bar through via a mount; the light can easily slid off the mount so you don't have to bike around with it during the day, nor leave it on the bike when it's parked outside.

text_fidelity_a:
SUGARBEAR'S Smart Weighted Hula Hoop Corset Waist Trimmer Waist Trainer Fitness Workout Plus Size Pop It Fidget (One Size, Smart Weighted Hula Hoop) This is the first “smart” weighted hula hoop I’ve used, so I can’t compare it first-hand to others, but I can say that I found this one very difficult to use. First off, I feel the product description is misleading. It states “24 detachable parts” which is correct, but that doesn’t mean 24 separate sections as I think is the case with most of these types of hula hoops. After doing some reading about other models, it seems most have 24 sections meaning it’s possible to customize the waist band to best fit your body. With this hula hoop, there are only 2 large sections and 5 additional, smaller sections. The smaller sections are 5”, so there’s no adjusting by a just a couple of inches. For me, that didn’t work. With an extra section added, the hula hoop was too big and tended to move around too much on my waist and end up at an angle rather than parallel with the floor. With a section taken out, it was too tight. There was no middle ground to fit me. And as far as adding and removing sections, it’s not easy. The pieces are difficult to get into place, and even more difficult to open back up. The sections snap together, then there are white pins that hold them together (these count for some of the advertised 24 pieces). The pins are very difficult to put in and take out, especially when the hula hoop is around your waist. The weight on this hula hoop is just a flimsy plastic bottle with a screw top that you need to fill with water or sand. The bottle arrived partially crushed, it was difficult to pop it back into shape, and when I filled it with water and secured the cap, it still leaked sending occasional drops of water flying. It’s up to the user to tie a knot to secure the rope on the end of the weight meaning the possibility exists the knot comes loose and the weight sails across the room. Other hula hoops I looked at have a clip to attach the weight. The hula hoop has a counter that keeps track of revolutions which is nice, but again, it appears other brands have trackers that do more and provide more options to monitor your workout.
Overall, the hula hoop does work, but it’s not very customizable and not very user friendly.
text_fidelity_b: SUGARBEAR'S Smart Weighted Hula Hoop Corset Waist Trimmer Waist Trainer Fitness Workout Plus Size Pop It Fidget (One Size, Smart Weighted Hula Hoop)

text_fidelity_a:
AMNQUERXUS Machine Washable Reflective Running Vest with LED Lights USB Rechargeable Safety Gear with Adjustable Waist, High Visibility Light Up Flashing Vest Gifts for Men Women Kids Dog Walking Sometimes where we live, it can get really scary when people drive by quickly and you are trying to go for a walk in the country to just relax. Having this vest handy is really a great item to put on both during the night time or dusk hours, or during hunting season to keep from being shot.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
CLOSURES
This comes with an XL vest that fits around the sides and closes. with strong velcro type closures.

FABRIC
This is a very nice mesh fabric. It allows for airflow and has a slight stretch/give to it so it is comfortable.

SIZING
This fits me and I am between a size 14 and 16 misses. If I were to put this over a winter jacket, I could still close it unless the coat is WAY too puffy.

HOW DOES THIS WORK?
POWER BOX
This is ingenious, actually. There is a little packet which recharges. It has a plug on it and also a cord that is USB to recharge it. Once it is charged, then you slip the little box unto a closed pocket which sits under a power button. The box gives a place for the power button to rest on when you press it.

LIGHTS
Once you have it connected, the button is pressed once, and you get the lights on front and back to go on. Once the lights are on, then you can make them flash fast by pressing another time. One more press makes for a slower blink, and a fourth press turns them off.

VEST
The vest itself is brilliant neon yellow. There is plenty of reflective tape all over this vest front and back. There is even a zipper pocket on the front for you to put your phone or other small items in.

BATTERY LIFE?
The battery life of this seems quite good. I have used it a few times and there is still no need for a recharge. I would say you could get a few hours of continuous use at least per charge, maybe more. My outings did not add up to that much yet.

WASHING
I am only going to handwash this without the battery pack and air dry it well before trying to use again. It will dry fast due to the fabric.

HUNTING SEASON
Around my area, fall time into winter can be dangerous. We have had our home shot by hunters by accident, and often there are inexperienced people who try to hunt and they don't pay attention to what is going on, thinking noises are deer. This vest will alert anyone in the early morning or early evening hours that there is a person there.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great vest to have handy. I plan to keep using this especially through hunting season and for late night walks when i hear a car coming.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is an ingenious little invention and I am glad to have it. I am considering purchasing others for the rest of the family.

I wanted something to keep my water cold and I didn't like how my metal water bottle was rattling on my bike.

This bottle is well insulated. It is not going to keep your water as cold as a metal water bottle, but the bottle fits much better the use in a bike. This is a great alternative to a metal bottle since it keeps the water colder than your typical plastic water bottle. It also has a really nice feel to it and easy to hold - the bottle is sort of squishy and not a very firm hard plastic. I also liked a feature so you can either use in the traditional mode (bottoms up) or you can switch it to use with a straw, which I thought was a plus. I tried both modes and it worked really well.

Overall, very happy with the bottle and hoping to get a lot of use out of it.

KUGOO Electric Scooter, 800W Motor Off-Road Scooter, 10-INCH Pneumatic Tires Up to 25 MPH Motorized Adult Scooter, Electric Scooter for Adults, Pro Scooter, G2 PRO I have 7 scooters I've collected along the way to review and hands down this is the most fun one out there! If you're familiar with how an electric scooter works then this one is just like the others and will be easy to setup and get going. Took me about five minutes to unbox and get going! Even for newbies this scooter is plenty easy to setup!

One of the favorite things I love on this are the giant wheels- we ride on a concrete trail several miles across town and this absolutely grabs onto the concrete very well and is a better overall ride! My one complaint is the tires must be thin as on my fourth ride, one of them got a flat even though I didn't hit anything noticeable like glass or a screw. Nothing in the tire but it just started losing pressure on a ride and within a couple minutes the tire was completely flat and I was stuck pushing it home a mile. My suggestion is to get the tire size off the tire and immediately swap them out for solid tires! The air tires are a slightly smoother ride but you'll regret it when you're stuck pushing it home...
Edit: The air leaks out of the valve stem. I went to add some green slime and it did hold air but when I moved the valve stem, air comes out at the bottom of it... So the valve stem was faulty and the slime didn't help anything. I've been searching like crazy with no luck finding a solid tire to replace these with. Should have been on the scooter to begin with in my opinion.

Speed wise, I got this monster up to 29 mph and I'm a larger man (260 pounds) so that's a testament to this thing! It stands higher than your average scooter too which is weird at first but I fell in love with the added height nearly instantly!

It has a faster startup than other scooters that require more of a kick start. Which- be careful, that can be dangerous if you have the scooter on and are pushing it to park it before turning it off. I almost flipped mine backwards onto myself this way, it happens QUICK. So definitely turn the scooter (and any scooter) off before pushing around.

Battery life is fantastic- we ride several miles across town and back and I still have half a battery left after that!

Overall this is my favorite thing I've gotten on review and I've gotten big fancy electronics like big TVs, computers, etc... But this is my favorite toy I've grabbed, I HIGHLY recommend it! In the future I'll absolutely be buying another from this company!

The bag is durable and sturdy, with soft lining on some inner pockets for things like a cell phone, GPS, or satellite link. text_fidelity_a:
NordicTrack T Series Treadmills My primary concerned based on other reviews was that the motor would be noisy. That depends entirely on the speed. If you want it as a walking treadmill, you will definitely hear your footfalls much louder. You could whisper above the motor, no problem. If you are a casual runner and want to take it to say 6 miles an hour (that's pretty much a 30 minute 5K) it's quiet. You can sort of hear it, but not a lot. If you are a pro athlete and want to take it to 10 miles an hour, first off, respect, and second off, you will hear noise about the equivalent to a car engine on the highway.

The iFit attachment, which I recommend, doesn't come with it. You need to buy it, and the subscription, separately. It enables you to download a series of training programs via WiFi including what may be the world's easiest C25K program. They call it Beginner 5K. It's 4 times a week for 12 weeks. It starts with you casually strolling along on the treadmill for half a mile in 15 minute (think the average walking pace of a senior citizen) but it ends with you running uphill at about 5 miles an hour (at that rate you could finish a 5K in roughly 40 minutes) and there are no sudden transitions. It just creeps up the incline a little, then the speed, and soon the fast pace of the old level is the resting pace of the new, but it feels like a resting pace. You build fitness gradually. The treadmill has some pre-programmed routes and workouts built in, and the site has a great many more. My only complaint is there is no way to preview the list before subscribing, to know if it's worth it. Set up for that was a bit of a pain, more so than I'd expected.

I found the left speaker a little weaker than the right, but that could be an audio trick used by Zombies, Run! Otherwise, the sound system is nice. It plugs in via a standard audio cable, not Blutooth in an era where standard audio cables are going out of fashion. There are adapters if that becomes an issue. There are holders for water and phone, etc, and a nice ledge for an ipad.

I like the cushioning, and it is adjustable. I like how easy it is to fold up. Mind, assemble this where you mean to keep it. You're not going to fold it and stuff it in a closet. It's way too heavy for that. Installation takes two people, especially at the end when you have to hold the bottom unit up to install the hydraulic lift. I needed to check a video for that part.

The off switch is to take the little key off the panel. You can use the reset button on the bottom, if you've set it up to be conveniently accessible, but it takes a lot longer to come back from that. It actually takes longer to come back from that, than from shutting of the surge protector it's plugged into, which makes me think it is doing some sort of reset processing. It definitely needs a surge protected, and I recommend the NordicTrack brand for this, just to be safe.

Overall, I'd say this is a high quality treadmill at a reasonable price.
text_fidelity_b: NordicTrack T Series Treadmills

text_fidelity_a:
Bowflex 4.1 Bench Black./Red This isn't our first FID (flat, incline, decline) bench, but while it has less features than some, it's exactly what we needed now. While our previous benches were rated for more weight and took more attachments, we like this one as it's lighter and smaller than the other ones - not light and small, exactly, as it is still rated for 450 pounds including user and weight, but still smaller. The foot holddown is adjustable, and while there aren't as many positions for the back as there are on some benches, including the newer version of this bench, there are enough. Also the seat adjusts, which wasn't true of the previous model, the 4.1.

We got this bench rather than the 5.1 version because we found a 4.1 we could actually try in person, and it was great for both my 6' 7" husband and me (i'm 5' 3"). The 5.1 version has the u-shaped front support, but the straight one on this bench works fine.

The only thing we don't love about it is that the gap between the seat and back is pretty wide in some positions, but that's normal with FID benches with thicker seats. Throw a towel between the two sections or cut a piece of foam out to the exact shape and slide whichever into the gap as needed.

We like our Bowflex SelectTech 4.1 bench a lot. It's stable, sturdy and does the job as long as you don't need a bench that is rated over 450 pounds total (which these days we don't need). It doesn't fold up, but it's smaller than a lot of the higher rated benches, and the foot holddown does the job well. If you're looking for a super light, small bench or a bench rated 600 pounds or more, this isn't the bench for you. If you're like us, under 250 pounds and wanting to work out with 200 pounds or less, this bench has the flexibility to enhance your workouts and the padding is pretty comfortable, too.
text_fidelity_b: Bowflex 4.1 Bench Black./Red

Swiss Cargo SCKJ02Q02 3 in 1 Kayak Carrier, Black I just got these (5/27/18) so I will be coming back to edit after next weekend when I use these for a two hour drive on the freeway, but for now I wanted to leave a review because of the 'screws not lining up' that I'm seeing on so many reviews.

I bought mine at Dunham's, which are already "seconds" so if anything I'd expect things like screws not quite lining up, but I think those reviewers just made the same assumption I did at first: that you install the two screws through the middle holes in the flat rubber bottom. That is incorrect!! The screws actually go in diagonal holes to form half of an X. I found that it really created a nice grip and being on a diagonal meant the maximum surface area possible of the attachy bit hugging my crossbars. So just an FYI - I wouldn't put a lot of stock in the "holes not lining up" reviews. One glance at the directions shows you how to properly attach the screws at opposite corners. Also note that the teeth on the middle bar may not tightly lock together right out of the box. Mine didn't. But then I realized that the red thing that locks them down also rotates to loosen or tighten those teeth together so now everything is good and locked.

EDIT: I'm back to give my review - I actually returned these. Problems I found: 1. the bottom of the J is flat instead of in the actual J shape. Seems like that would make it easier to load but it doesn't because if you put it in the center of your roof to use with two kayaks it is pretty far from the edge of your roof so lifting the kayak into the holder becomes difficult just due to how much roof you have to clear before you reach the rack, and sliding the kayak on from the rear doesn't work either because of the flat instead of actual J design, so there is nothing holding your kayak onto the device when you slide it up onto the roof and it just falls over the side of the car. You need someone else to at least spot the kayak to make sure it doesn't fall so this carrier requires two people.

The second issue is that it is very small. If you have two little 8 footers it should be fine but if you have an Old Towne or a Wilderness or really any brand of fishing kayak you are only going to be able to fit one in this holder because without that J shape you have to lean the center bracket way back to hold your wider kayak without it plunging back to the ground before you can ever get it fastened up.

The one thing I liked was the way it attached to the cross bars. That diagonal design AND the way they designed it so one side has a typical screw hole but the other side is a non-closed hole so you can screw on both bolts and then swing the underneath 'arm' onto the second bolt and tighten to your crossbars, makes it easier than trying to start the screw/bolt from completely unattached while on a roof of a car. It's hard to explain without seeing it, but you'll have to take my word that it's a nice feature the makers obviously considered when designing the product.

It did hold my kayak securely (with the center bar at about 145 degrees), I just didn't see a point in keeping a holder for two kayaks when it would only hold one of my kayak's size. I used these on ROLA aftermarket crossbars, aero shaped 3.5", found here on Amazon and it fit very well on those bars. Construction I would say is excellent.
text_fidelity_b: Swiss Cargo SCKJ02Q02 3 in 1 Kayak Carrier, Black

Sector 9 Tempest Drop Through Top Mount Complete Skateboard, Assorted I bought this from seller Amazon April 2017. I received the tri-color (raw, orange, blue) trucks, and the board and wheels as pictured at this date. This skateboard is a lot of fun.

The skateboard is Sector 9 brand. Sector 9 was an early-adopter and innovator of long-board and cruiser technology, and I think it's fair to say they continue to be leaders in those markets. This board has the double-standard kingpin trucks that allow it to carve a tighter radius than boards with single standard or reverse kingpin trucks of the same wheelbase. These ultra-flexy trucks allow a longer wheelbase to carve like a shorter board.

This board is in the Sidewinder series, meaning it has the Sidewinder II trucks. The Surfwinder series also has these trucks, but that series has more traditional surfboard shape decks, without cut-outs, and therefore smaller wheels. Among similar Sidewinder series boards, this Tempest has a tail, whereas the Fractal doesn't really. The Horizon also has a tail, and is a little longer and wider overall. The Striker has a very similar board shape and size, but the deck is vertically laminated bamboo and fiberglass, whereas the Tempest is 7-ply maple.

I chose this board because of the Sidewinder trucks first, then the large wheels (compared to Surfwinder series for example). The pavement in my small rural town is pretty neglected, and big wheels help overcome some of the cracks. Others can swallow car tires.

I'll write more later...
text_fidelity_b: Sector 9 Tempest Drop Through Top Mount Complete Skateboard, Assorted

text_fidelity_a:
iClimb Heavy Duty Hard Arm Camping Folding Mesh Chair with Cup Holder, Bottle Opener and Carry Bag Guys, now this is the real deal! It is far from the standard, wimpy, light weight chairs you're used to seeing set up around camp fires or out on the soccer field sidelines. I am incredibly impressed.
The metal feels incredibly strong and durable. It's a very thick and heavy frame. If a kid or klutzy adult (like myself) were to bump hard into one of the arms or legs when someone was someone was sitting in it, it could easily leave a bruise. I'm not trying to suggest this chair isn't safe, but rather trying to convey just how heavy duty this metal frame is. Plus, the material the seat is made out of is very thick too. It also looks incredibly durable and like it should last a long time. I haven't had a reason to wash this chair yet, but I see no reason why this material wouldn't be easy clean if it needed it. Oh, and it is much more comfortable to sit in than the other chairs. The sturdiness helps an awful lot.
So overall, I really do like it. But because it is so "heavy duty" it is a heavy chair! Especially when to compared to what a standard folding chair weighs. I can't say for sure, but I suspect this chair probably weighs around twice as much as the average camping chair. Which probably isn't a big deal if you're not having to carry it a very long way. But lets say I had to hike quite a ways to a camping site (with the weight of all the other gear on my back too), well then I would think twice about choosing this chair. Oh and it is taller than most too. I would say it's about six inches taller then the standard folding chair.
So overall, I defiantly think this is an impressive, well made chair. I am 5'6 and a 150 pounds, so I already fit "comfortably" in a standard camping chair. For me personally, unless I had severe back pain or some other painful condition, I don't think I personally would NEED this chair. I still really like it and would prefer to sit in it, but a chair this heavy duty wouldn't be necessity for me. My 250 lb hubby on the other hand would completely disagree. He is VERY comfortable sitting in this chair. He also probably wouldn't noticed the extra length or weight of this chair if he had to carry it folded up on his back. Hands down, he would most certainly prefer this chair over the standard type of camping chair. It really is that nice. We both would recommend it. I'm even saving this as an idea to get my own dad for next Father's day!
text_fidelity_b: iClimb Heavy Duty Hard Arm Camping Folding Mesh Chair with Cup Holder, Bottle Opener and Carry Bag

Due to the blaze red/orange painted tops, during daylight hours they really stand out on the surface of the water.  Also, they are very noticeable as the light wanes in the evening or early hours of the day.  Without adequate weight below them, they will lay over on their side. The larger floats stand quite high off the water with small split shots for ballast. For the price, they are a pretty good buy and I think they will perform well for Crappie or sunfish. The bottom is where the eye is located and it can break with casting abuse.  The eye of the float will need some probing, as most are not a completely pierced hole and will need some attention with the point of a hook. I hate all of the hydroflask brand lids. The twist coffee lids have tendency to failure in my opinion, the screw lids are not great if you like to take sips often, and the straw lids are actually not bad, but sometimes, you just don't want a straw. This lid is a great alternative if you want a simple one-handed open close that's still strong enough that it won't open by accident.

Pros
-easy one handed open
-if you look closely at the pictures there is a textured rubber grip that makes grabbing it from the top a more secure feeling
-the moveable handle is nice
-Many other 3rd party lids are either too tight (hard to open) or too loose (prone to accidental openings and leaks). But this one is perfectly right in the middle. It's easy to open one handed, but still fairly secure to resist accidental openings.

Cons:
Like most of these snap lids, the trade-off is slightly less insulation then the HydroFlask brand lids. When I did a side-by side test with several of my Hydro Flask lids, this Takeya melted ice faster than the hydroflask. This is still not too bad as the water was still cold, just not quite as cold as a stock hydroflask lid

Who this is for: You want a more convenient drinking experience and hate the Hydro Flask brand options. Good for one-handed open/close

Who this isn't for: If you must have long-lasting ice in your container for as much time as possible.

Wald Steel Handlebar #803 5.25" 27" 1" Black These are a good product for the price. I purchased them to give myself a little more upright position on an old mountain bike. They do this pretty well.

The reason they do not get 5 stars is the top portion where you put your hand was about 3/4 of an inch too short to mount my original twist shifters and still have room for my grips, making the place where you put your hands a little shorter than intended. OK for me, and also wouldn't be an issue for maybe a different type shifter - like the trigger type, or no shifter at all like a single speed bike. However for someone with very large hands it might be a problem.

Beyond that they appear to be pretty decent quality for the price.

Don't underestimate the amount of change in position that you will get. I paired these with a adjustable quill stem, and I think one or the other would be sufficient, so if your changing out an old mountain bike I might start with one or the other, not both. Also, due to the longer reach you will very likely need to change your shifter and brake cables. My originals were cut too short for this handlebar. Its not a difficult job, but a fair bit of work. You probably will want to buy new grips also in case your originals like mine were hard to remove.
text_fidelity_b: Wald Steel Handlebar #803 5.25" 27" 1" Black

text_fidelity_a:
Compaclite High Back Oversize Steel Portable Chair for Outdoor Camping / Picnic / Hiking / Bicycling / Fishing / BBQ / Beach / Patio with Carry Bag, Royal Blue I’m torn with how to rate this chair. I have the 360 swivel version ($60) as well as this one, which is about half the price. This compaclite chair has a higher back which makes it more comfortable than the swivel version, and the pillow actually is a nice plus. It’s compact and more comfortable than typical folding chairs. When compared to the swivel version, this one wins no contest. However, it still isn’t enough for it to be bumped up to 5 stars, and I’ll tell you why.

As many others have mentioned, these chairs aren’t the sturdiest and wobble a bit. The drink holder is placed in an awkward place on the chair (right between your legs) and the chair does take a few minutes to set up, whereas a simple folding chair is done in a few seconds. I imagine this will get better with time, but it does take some elbow grease to get the corners of the chair into the poles. Although the pillow is quite comfortable and really nice, it makes folding the chair a bit more of a pain that the swivel version (because no pillow). One of compaclite’s best features is the fact that…yes…it’s compact, so the pillow adds a stressor that makes it difficult to be easily compact. I struggled for a solid 5 minutes to get this one in the bag.

Ultimately, it comes down to what you value. Do you need something that turns in a circle? Do you want arm rests? Do you want a pillow? Should it be compact? Do you want something that can be easily set up? If you are searching for a compact chair that can easily be carried and don’t mind set-up and break down times, then I would recommend this chair. Otherwise, you might want to look elsewhere if those aren’t your priorities.
text_fidelity_b: Compaclite High Back Oversize Steel Portable Chair for Outdoor Camping / Picnic / Hiking / Bicycling / Fishing / BBQ / Beach / Patio with Carry Bag, Royal Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Cilkus Bicycle Pump with Pressure Gauge. Mini Portable Bicycle Pump Compatible with Presta and Schrader Valve Bicycles, Including air Bag Needle and Free Puncture Repair I had a tiny little hand pump and a giant full sized floor pump. I needed something to ride along with my on my bike. So I chose to go with a CO2 canister and this mini floor foot pump. When I saw how small it was, I didn't think it was going to be that effective. Especially with the tires that I'm blowing up. I'm running 26x4 fat tires and there's a lot of volume going on in there. Hopefully, I'll be moving to smaller tubes once I install some tannus armor. In the mean time, I needed more volume than the hand pump could provide and a something more portable than the floor pump.
I tested this out by dropping a tire from 30PSI to 20PSI. The chuck went on solid and locked without issue. The good news is that this pump does move air. The fact that I could see the needle move on the pressure gauge was a good indication of effectiveness. The none gauge version would have been nice for portability, but being able to read pressure on the fly is pretty necessary for me. Also the pump retainer/ foot hold works great for stabilizing the pump.

Things that don't work for me. I don't like that the hose comes out the side. It makes in harder to store.
I would have a like a pressure bleeder valve. And most importantly, the chuck leaks with taking it off. So you have to add more pressure than you planned on and you'd need another gauge that doesn't bleed to read the pressure afterwards.

Overall, while it could use some improvement, it's still a great little tool to have in an emergency. Or even if you want to soften the tires for off road and then pump them back up for the asphalt.
text_fidelity_b: Cilkus Bicycle Pump with Pressure Gauge. Mini Portable Bicycle Pump Compatible with Presta and Schrader Valve Bicycles, Including air Bag Needle and Free Puncture Repair

text_fidelity_a: Meade 81015 Spotting Scope (Black) There are a number of things to consider when buying a spotting scope -- none of which I knew before buying this one.  One thing is MINIMUM focus.  For many this may not be an issue but for indoor target range shooting at 25 feet I cannot see 22 caliber hits in the bullseye and so I bought this.  Unfortunately the minimum focus distance is 28 feet.  Another factor is "eye relief" which is how close your eyeball needs to be to the focusing element -- in this case, very close -- which is an issue when I have my regular glasses plus safety glasses over them and as a result I cannot get close enough to the focusing element.  Some have criticized the tripod -- I agree that it is pretty cheap, especially when legs are extended.  However, for bench use without the legs extended the footprint is just 10x10x10 and height to the eyepiece is 20 inches.  It's plenty stable and just the right height.  As others have mentioned, the case is excellent.  After the little research I did, I ended up buying a Nikon Prostaff 5 at about $370.  Pricey compared to the Meade but far superior.  Focuses to 13 feet, has significant eye relief so I can use it without removing my glasses, and is much brighter.
text_fidelity_b: Meade 81015 Spotting Scope (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Weaver Leather Throw Line Storage Bag Are you a ham radio operator tossing portable antennas up into trees? Don't like the idea of sling shots and potato launchers? Hate that tangled mess of mason line? Looking for reasonable elevation for the weekend? I recommend this.

I hate rope, string, wine, wire, cable, and anything squiggly that is over 25 feet long. It is certain to become a tangled mess and cost 30 minutes to an hour to straighten out just to have it wrap around your ankle and trip you up. Happens to me every single time.

Some smart ham out there suggested I try this throw line bag and weight. After it was delivered I brought it out to the backyard and started tossing it around. I made about five or six long low tosses without any tangles and three or four high tosses over the tree without a problem. I'm sold on it. My slingshot is going to see a lot less use and I still don't have the guts to try my potato launcher.

The bag is more than storage. After a toss you just stuff the line back in the bag without concern for winding it properly. Just push it down in the bag. When tossing the weight you just let the line play out of the bag. I have yet to experience a tangle. I'm sure there's some added resistance and I might be losing a foot or two of max height but for ease of storage and deployment you can have the foot.

When done, stuff the line in the bag along with the weight. Cinch it up and toss back in the truck until next time. Not a whole lot of fussing.

A warning... wear gloves. The rope they use burns! Me and one other person found out the hard way. Ya... I didn't tell him. But even after that he went out and bought his own kit so maybe the burn wasn't so bad. Still, wear gloves.

I think I got the 12 oz weight. Then next one down might have been a little better. After a few tosses of the 12 oz weight I was getting real tired and my height/distance was dropping rapidly. Good argument for doing it right the first time I guess. Still, 8 oz might be some benefit.

I know it's tempting but don't toss this thing at your buddies. The weight is substantial and if you hit them they won't share in your amusement. Not that I did anything like that but you know. It could happen.

That's it. Wish I found this a long time ago. Until now I had been using my slingshot with a 1 oz weight and a Zebco 33 and 20 lb test line. Then I would tie the mason line for the second pass. The tangles were unbelievable so a spool of mason line was a one-time-use item for me. The rope in this kit is strong enough to hold up any wire antenna for a weekend so you only need a single pass.
text_fidelity_b: Weaver Leather Throw Line Storage Bag

Compass/divider sets easily and holds firmly. No screw mechanism -- simply pull/push to adjust.

Very sharp points on divider - perfect for measurement work.
Ruling pen and optional holder: I like line work in my field journal, and this makes gorgeous lines with watercolor or ink. Purchased separately, a ruling pen is about $8 USD.

Additional lead in tube -- nice touch!

What I didn't like...
Absolutely no instructions whatsoever, BUT the tools are intuitive for anyone who has ever used engineering/math compass sets.
A drop point attachment would have been more useful in this kit than an extension bar. (Drop points allow a compass to draw tiny circles smaller than the radius with the compass fully closed.)
